agreement: Executed Credit Agreement (Veyrona 2025 Senior Secured Credit Facility) among Veyrona Decision Systems, LLC, as Borrower; Veyron Holdings, LLC, as Guarantor/co-Grantor; and Granite Harbor Direct Lending, LP, as Administrative Agent and sole Lender. Issued January 10, 2025; effective/closing January 15, 2025; matures January 15, 2030. $250,000,000 total commitment = $187,274,929.89 funded term loan + $62,725,070.11 undrawn revolver (Schedule 1.1), refinancing $179,250,000 of legacy debt at closing. Only the Maximum Net Leverage Ratio threshold steps down, each amendment paired with one small bundled accommodation.

Covenant_EBITDA.verbatim: Net Leverage Ratio means Net Debt divided by trailing-four-quarter Covenant EBITDA.

agreement_ref.quote: Net Leverage Ratio means Net Debt divided by trailing-four-quarter Covenant EBITDA.

Covenant_EBITDA.note: GENUINE DEFINITIONAL GAP, not a transcription omission: Article I of the Original Credit Agreement (the entirety of the Definitions article is three sentences) never states an EBITDA computation formula or an add-back limb of any kind -- it only NAMES 'Covenant EBITDA' as an input to the Net Leverage Ratio. There is no 'net income plus interest, taxes, D&A' starting formula, no 'adjusted only for permitted, documented items' limiter (contrast a sibling facility in this portfolio whose agreement carries exactly that limiting phrase), and no deemed/stipulated EBITDA schedule (full-text search of every executed document for 'deemed', 'shall be deemed', 'stipulated', 'agreed EBITDA' and 'add-back' returned zero matches). In practice, every one of the six quarterly Covenant_Calculation workbooks filed 2025 Q1 through 2026 Q2 shows 'Permitted add-backs: $0' and 'Reported operating EBITDA' tying exactly to 'Covenant EBITDA' (Tie-to-leverage-summary residual = 0 every quarter), and the FY2024 Reviewed Financial Statements independently show Revenue $213,000,000.00 - Cost of revenue $115,020,000.00 - Operating expenses $64,519,339.31 = Covenant EBITDA $33,460,660.69 exactly, with no add-back line on the statement's face. Bound here to the model's single pinned EBITDA bridge row ('Reported EBITDA', per borrower-config model_lines.ebitda_bridge) on the strength of that six-quarter-and-FY2024 evidence -- but because the agreement itself supplies no textual limiter, there is no contractual guardrail against a future borrower-proposed add-back the way a 'documented items only' clause would provide. No deemed_schedule: none exists in this agreement.

Funded_Debt.note: Balance-sheet principal balance of the facility (borrower-config model_lines.total_debt = 'Funded Debt'). Through Q2 2026 this is the term loan only, amortizing 0.60%/month -- every certified quarterly Funded Debt figure (Q1'25 $183,924,166.39 through Q2'26 $168,048,469.80) is consistent with zero revolver draws to date; the $62,725,070.11 revolver commitment stays excluded as undrawn per this defined term. If the revolver draws, the model row's balance should rise accordingly.

Unrestricted_Cash.note: The borrower's monthly Balance Sheet carries a single 'Cash' line with no separate restricted-cash balance disclosed in any period reviewed (Jan 2025 - Jun 2026) -- treated as fully unrestricted absent evidence otherwise. Verified: the Balance Sheet 'Cash' figure at each fiscal-quarter-end month ties exactly to the corresponding Covenant_Calculation workbook's 'Less: Unrestricted Cash' line (e.g. March 2025 Balance Sheet Cash $9,998,329.80 = Q1 2025 Covenant Calculation 'Unrestricted Cash' $9,998,329.80).

Net_Debt.verbatim: Net Leverage Ratio means Net Debt divided by trailing-four-quarter Covenant EBITDA. [Net Debt itself is never independently defined as a subtraction formula anywhere in the agreement -- it is only introduced by this sentence, immediately followed by the Funded Debt and Unrestricted Cash sentences below it in the same three-sentence Article I.]

agreement_ref.quote: Net Leverage Ratio means Net Debt divided by trailing-four-quarter Covenant EBITDA. Funded Debt excludes undrawn commitments. Unrestricted Cash excludes restricted cash.

Net_Debt.note: ENGINE-DESIGN NOTE for build-monitoring-model, matching the established pattern used elsewhere in this portfolio for the identical issue: Net Debt is contractually a SUBTRACTION (Funded Debt less Unrestricted Cash) but the covenant engine's 'formula' compute supports only op:'sum' (an unsupported op raises loudly), so it cannot express Funded_Debt minus Unrestricted_Cash directly. This definition is instead bound to a model_line named 'Net Debt' that build-monitoring-model must add to the assembled model as Funded Debt minus Cash. VERIFIED against all six Covenant_Calculation workbooks filed to date (2025 Q1 through 2026 Q2): 'Net Debt' = 'Funded Debt' - 'Less: Unrestricted Cash' exactly every quarter, with both 'Debt check' and 'Ratio check' residual lines equal to 0.00 in every filing -- this is the best-evidenced reading available given the agreement's own text never spells out the subtraction in so many words. RUN-LOCAL BINDING FIX (2026-09-16, covenant-compliance module run for 2026-06): the assembled model's actual Balance Sheet row for this figure is titled 'Net Debt (derived: Funded Debt - Cash)', not the bare 'Net Debt' this note calls for (same derived-row naming convention as this borrower's 'Gross Profit (derived)' row) -- the original binding raised 'model line Net Debt not found in model' for every test date. Repointed compute.model_line to the model's actual label IN THIS RUN'S OWN covenant-spec.json SNAPSHOT ONLY (not the canonical .record/current copy) after verifying the row ties EXACTLY to every quarter's certified Funded Debt/Unrestricted Cash/Net Debt figures. Flagged as an exception for covenant-setup or build-monitoring-model to correct at the data layer (rename the model row to bare 'Net Debt', or update the canonical spec's binding to match) so future runs do not need this repoint.

step7_signoff.decided_by: onboarding session (auto-decided per analyst's standing instruction not to pause for confirmation during this batch onboarding; every decision below is flagged for prompt analyst review given this borrower's amendment/restatement complexity)

decisions.question: The agreement's '0.60% of beginning principal monthly' phrase is ambiguous between flat-off-original-principal (what the v1 debt-service engine models) and declining balance (0.60% of each month's own opening balance). The borrower's own 18 straight months of certified Debt & Liquidity figures resolve this as declining balance, and the generated schedule is already ~5.2% too high cumulative by June 2026, growing every month after.
options_considered: Accept as parsed: use the generated (flat) schedule's principal/balance figures as specified
Bind to the borrower's own certified Debt & Liquidity tab figures directly, since they are demonstrably the true declining-balance mechanic
decisions.decision: Bind Funded_Debt and any principal/balance figure used downstream to the borrower's certified Debt & Liquidity tab (and the model's own Funded Debt row built from it), NOT the generated debt-service-schedule's principal/balance figures.
decisions.rationale: This mirrors the same decision already made for a sibling facility in this portfolio with the identical ambiguous amortization clause and the identical engine gap. The generated schedule is a known, quantified flat-base approximation; the certified figures tie to a real declining-balance mechanic in every one of 18 months checked. Since the sole covenant here is a leverage test (not a coverage test), this decision affects the Funded_Debt/Net_Debt inputs directly, not a Fixed_Charges formula.

decisions.question: No executed document states any interest rate, index, margin, or PIK mechanic, and the borrower's own monthly packages carry no interest-expense line to reverse-engineer a rate from -- a genuine drafting gap, not merely an omission from this data room. The debt-service engine requires a non-zero rate to generate a schedule at all.
options_considered: Refuse to generate a debt-service schedule at all until a real rate is sourced

Generate the schedule with a clearly-labeled 1bp non-contractual placeholder rate, so the schedule's shape (amortization, maturity) is still usable while every cash-interest figure is understood to be void
decisions.decision: Accept the 1bp placeholder rate for schedule generation, but flag every cash-interest figure derived from it as VOID and non-contractual until the true rate is confirmed directly with Granite Harbor Direct Lending, LP.
decisions.rationale: The sole covenant is a leverage test with no Fixed Charges/coverage component, so no covenant verdict in this batch depends on the interest rate. Generating a schedule with a labeled placeholder preserves the amortization and maturity shape for reference while making the interest gap impossible to miss, rather than blocking the whole debt-service-spec on a term the executed documents simply do not contain. This is the single highest-priority open item for the analyst to resolve directly with the lender.

decisions.question: The cloud-migration capex basket (First Amendment) and customer-data-license investment basket (Second Amendment) both carry no dollar cap, percentage-of-EBITDA limit, or expiration date anywhere in the executed text. Should an informal monitoring cap be imposed for tracking purposes?
options_considered: Leave both as reference-only negative-covenant entries with no tested primitive and no informal cap
Impose an analyst-elected informal cap (e.g., a round dollar figure) purely for monitoring purposes
decisions.decision: Leave both as reference-only entries, untracked against any numeric limit.
decisions.rationale: Neither amendment states a cap of any kind. Fabricating an informal monitoring threshold the agreement itself does not impose would create a false sense of a bright-line test where none exists, and could cause the monitor to flag a covenant breach that has no contractual basis. Both baskets are captured in the spec so the analyst knows they exist and can ask the borrower for actual usage if material capex or investment activity appears in the financials.

decisions.question: The Third Amendment's 'revised-reporting controls' (traded for revolver preservation) names no specific deliverable, cadence, or format anywhere in the executed text.
options_considered: Accept as parsed: record as an open, undefined affirmative obligation with no way to test satisfaction
Assume it is already satisfied by the existing monthly package and AR-aging cadence
decisions.decision: Accept as parsed: record as an open, undefined affirmative obligation. Do not assume satisfaction.
decisions.rationale: The executed text gives no basis to conclude what would satisfy this obligation, so neither declaring it met nor unmet is well-supported. Flagging it as an open item for the analyst to raise directly with the lender is the honest reading, especially since the bundled consideration (revolver preservation) is a real, valuable accommodation the borrower received for an obligation whose content is undefined.

decisions.question: The agreement requires the borrower to 'promptly' identify any restatement and affected period, with no day-count defined. The March 2026 restatement notice is dated 2026-06-20, roughly three months after the affected period.
options_considered: Record a view on whether ~3 months satisfies 'promptly'
Record the gap neutrally with no verdict on Event-of-Default classification
decisions.decision: Record the gap neutrally: the fact and the elapsed time, with no verdict on whether it satisfies 'promptly'.
decisions.rationale: The agreement's own text supplies no day-count or standard against which to judge timeliness, so asserting a breach or compliance would be a legal conclusion this spec is not positioned to make. The fact is preserved for the analyst's and, if needed, counsel's own judgment.

decisions.question: The Q1 2026 compliance certificate (signed 2026-04-12) was never re-issued after the March 2026 restatement was discovered (notice dated 2026-06-20); it certifies pre-restatement EBITDA. No standalone corrected Q1 2026 certificate exists anywhere in the deal folder.
options_considered: Treat the as-filed Q1 2026 certificate as the final word for that quarter
Treat it as superseded-but-never-reissued, and read Q1 2026 (for trend/cross-check purposes going forward) off the corrected TTM Build figures embedded in the Q2 2026 workbook
decisions.decision: Treat the Q1 2026 certificate as superseded-but-never-reissued; covenant-compliance and the monitor should read Q1 2026's corrected figures from the Q2 2026 workbook's TTM Build tab for trend purposes, while still reporting the as-filed certified figure as the historical certified-of-record value for that quarter.
decisions.rationale: The compliance verdict does not change either way (5.1265x as-filed vs. 5.1200x corrected, both under the 5.25x threshold then in effect), so this is a documentation-hygiene question, not a covenant-outcome question. Reporting both figures, with the corrected one used for trend continuity, is more transparent than silently substituting one for the other or ignoring the gap.

decisions.question: Article IX references 'stated cure periods' generically, but no actual cure-period length or equity-cure mechanism is spelled out anywhere for this specific covenant.
options_considered: Accept as parsed: no cure right exists for this covenant
Infer a market-standard cure period despite the absence of specific text
decisions.decision: Accept as parsed: no cure right.
decisions.rationale: Inferring a cure mechanism the agreement does not actually spell out would overstate the borrower's contractual protection. Absent explicit cure-period language for this covenant, none is assumed.

open_items_for_analyst: HIGHEST PRIORITY: confirm the facility's true interest rate, index/margin, and day-count convention directly with Granite Harbor Direct Lending, LP -- no executed document states any of this, and the generated debt-service schedule's cash-interest figures are void placeholders until a real rate is sourced.
Confirm whether the Third Amendment's 'revised-reporting controls' obligation has been defined or satisfied in any side correspondence not in this deal folder.

Ask the borrower for actual usage/dollar activity under the two unquantified baskets (cloud-migration capex, customer-data-license investment) if material capex or investment line items appear in the financials.
No re-signed Q1 2026 compliance certificate exists after the March 2026 restatement was discovered -- consider requesting one from the borrower for the file, even though the verdict does not change.

The executed Third Amendment settled at a looser 5.00x threshold than its own unsigned April 1, 2026 draft's proposed 4.75x -- the negotiation history behind that change is not documented in this deal folder and may be worth asking the deal team about directly.

Covenant headroom has compressed from ~13% (Q1 2025) to ~2% (Q2 2026) across three tightening amendments even as absolute leverage and EBITDA have been roughly stable-to-improving -- each amendment has cut the ceiling faster than operating performance has improved it. This is the central credit story for this borrower going into the next several test dates.
